claim: The parser keeps a slot count (`arity` / token count) but the game only reads a prefix of it, and a MISSING slot is filled from the statement defaults rather than rejected -- so neither `ucontrol move x y` (four fields, not six) nor a short `op` line is a defect.
why: LExecutor.java:344-352 — `case move, stop, approach, pathfind` reads x,y and (only for `approach`) a radius. The `p1..p4` toNumber() calls happen before dispatch, so `uses` is always 1,2,3 even when nothing reads them. Reporting a missing/extra slot against `arity` flags correct community code. Same class on the `op` side (2026-10-27, user asked for the false-positive WARN to be removed): LStatement default read() leaves absent fields at their declared defaults (LStatements.java:708-711 `OperationStatement.dest = "result", a = "a", b = "b"`), so `op add r 1`, `op add` and `op abs` each compile to a real OpI -- v160.7 jar: `op add r 1` -> [OpI] with r=1 (the absent operand reads null and adds as 0), `op abs` -> [OpI]. The old `WARN op abs given 1 args, expects 2` was therefore a pure false positive and is gone; an unknown operator NAME is still ERR (`unknown-op`).
state: silent -- both slot-count reports are false positives and no checker emits them any more (ucontrol move: the executor reads a prefix of `arity`; op: absent slots fall back to the statement defaults and still build a real instruction)
